/-!
# Conjecture 6.3

by R. Bieri

A group $G$ is called *of type $(FP)_{\infty}$* if the trivial $G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
resolution by finitely generated projective $G$-modules. The class of all groups of type
$(FP)_{\infty}$ has a couple of excellent closure properties with respect to extensions and
amalgamated products (R. Bieri, *Homological dimension of discrete groups*, Queen Mary College
Math. Notes, London, 1976). Is every periodic group of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ finite? This is
related to the question whether there is an infinite periodic group with a finite presentation.

Here a $G$-module is a module over the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$, formalised as
`MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`, and a periodic group is one in which every element has finite order
(`Monoid.IsTorsion`).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

justification.why_needed: The trivial ℤG-module ℤ as an object of `ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G)`, needed as the object being resolved. Defined as `ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule` (an abbrev, so it is just a packaging of Mathlib notions).

blocks.name: trivialModule
blocks.text:
/-- The trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$, on which every element of $G$ acts as the
identity, as an object of the category of `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`-modules. -/
noncomputable abbrev trivialModule (G : Type) [Group G] : ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) :=
  ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *of type $(FP)_{\infty}$* if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$
has a resolution $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ by finitely generated projective
$\mathbb{Z}G$-modules $P_n$. Here a resolution is a `CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution`: a
chain complex of projective `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`-modules together with a quasi-isomorphism to
$\mathbb{Z}$ placed in degree $0$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution` / `HasProjectiveResolution` (no finite-generation condition); `Rep.barResolution`/standard resolution (a specific, non-f.g. resolution); `Module.FinitePresentation` (only FP_1-level, for modules not groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.3».IsTypeFPInfty
justification.why_needed: Type (FP)_∞ is not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Defined per the statement: ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution (trivialModule G), ∀ n, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X n), i.e. a (possibly infinite) resolution of ℤ by finitely generated projective ℤG-modules. Restricted to `G : Type` so that the resolution lives in `ModuleCat.{0}`; since f.g. modules over a Type-0 ring are small this loses no generality, and the conjecture quantifies over `G : Type` anyway.

blocks.name: IsTypeFPInfty
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *of type $(FP)_{\infty}$* if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$
has a resolution $\cdots \to P_1 \to P_0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ by finitely generated projective
$\mathbb{Z}G$-modules $P_n$. Here a resolution is a `CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution`: a
chain complex of projective `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`-modules together with a quasi-isomorphism to
$\mathbb{Z}$ placed in degree $0$. -/
def IsTypeFPInfty (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ P : ProjectiveResolution (trivialModule G),
    ∀ n, Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X n)

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators and
finitely many relators, i.e. to `PresentedGroup rels` for some finite set `rels` of elements
of the free group on `Fin n`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Group.FG` (only finite generation), `PresentedGroup` (a construction, not a predicate), `Algebra.FinitePresentation` (for algebras, not groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.3».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has `PresentedGroup` and `Group.FG` but no predicate 'G is finitely presented'. Defined as ∃ n, ∃ rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)), Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G). Two proved `@[category API]` lemmas (presented groups with finitely many relators are finitely presented; invariance under `MulEquiv`) are included as basic tests.

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators and
finitely many relators, i.e. to `PresentedGroup rels` for some finite set `rels` of elements
of the free group on `Fin n`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

noncomputable def trivialModuleUnitEquiv :
    MonoidAlgebra ℤ Unit ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra ℤ Unit]
      (Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModule :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective
    (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton _ _ ((Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv.symm 1)) (by
    constructor
    · intro r s h
      simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply] at h
      apply_fun (Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv at h
      simp only [Representation.asModuleEquiv_map_smul] at h
      simp [Representation.asAlgebraHom_def, MonoidAlgebra.lift_apply, Representation.trivial] at h
      rw [Finsupp.sum_fintype _ _ (fun _ => rfl), Finsupp.sum_fintype _ _ (fun _ => rfl)] at h
      simp only [Fintype.sum_unique] at h
      exact Finsupp.ext fun i => by cases i; exact h
    · intro z
      refine ⟨MonoidAlgebra.single ()
        ((Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv z), ?_⟩
      simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply]
      apply_fun (Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv using LinearEquiv.injective _
      simp only [Representation.asModuleEquiv_map_smul]
      simp)
blocks.docstring:
The group ring $\mathbb{Z}[1]$ of the trivial group is isomorphic, as a module over itself,
to the trivial module $\mathbb{Z}$ via $r \mapsto r \cdot 1$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Representation.asModuleEquiv` (only ℤ-linear, not ℤ[G]-linear) and `MonoidAlgebra` algebra isomorphisms for the trivial monoid (none found giving the required module isomorphism directly).
justification.name: Kourovka.«6.3».trivialModuleUnitEquiv
justification.why_needed: Auxiliary linear isomorphism ℤ[1] ≃ₗ[ℤ[1]] ℤ used only in the `@[category test]` lemma `isTypeFPInfty_unit`, which verifies that `IsTypeFPInfty` is satisfiable (the trivial group is of type (FP)_∞) and hence that the hypothesis of the main conjecture is not vacuous.

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isTypeFPInfty_unit : IsTypeFPInfty Unit := by
  haveI : Projective (trivialModule Unit) :=
    ModuleCat.projective_of_free
      ((Module.Basis.singleton Unit (MonoidAlgebra ℤ Unit)).map trivialModuleUnitEquiv)
  refine ⟨ProjectiveResolution.self _, fun n => ?_⟩
  cases n with
  | zero => exact Module.Finite.equiv trivialModuleUnitEquiv
  | succ n =>
    have : Subsingleton ((ProjectiveResolution.self (trivialModule Unit)).complex.X (n + 1)) :=
      ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
        (HomologicalComplex.isZero_single_obj_X _ _ _ _ (by simp))
    infer_instance

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H)
    (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : IsFinitelyPresented H :=
  let ⟨n, rels, ⟨f⟩⟩ := hG
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨f.trans e⟩⟩
blocks.docstring: Being finitely presented is invariant under group isomorphism.
blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv
blocks.text:
/-- Being finitely presented is invariant under group isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H)
    (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : IsFinitelyPresented H :=
  let ⟨n, rels, ⟨f⟩⟩ := hG
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨f.trans e⟩⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  refine Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range (e ∘ PresentedGroup.of), ?_, Set.finite_range _⟩
  rw [Set.range_comp, ← MonoidHom.coe_coe, ← MonoidHom.map_closure,
    PresentedGroup.closure_range_of, ← MonoidHom.range_eq_map, MonoidHom.range_eq_top]
  exact e.surjective
blocks.docstring: A finitely presented group is finitely generated.
blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented.fg

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  refine Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range (e ∘ PresentedGroup.of), ?_, Set.finite_range _⟩
  rw [Set.range_comp, ← MonoidHom.coe_coe, ← MonoidHom.map_closure,
    PresentedGroup.closure_range_of, ← MonoidHom.range_eq_map, MonoidHom.range_eq_top]
  exact e.surjective

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G → (G is of type FP_∞) → Finite G; 'periodic' means every element has finite order (Mathlib `Monoid.IsTorsion`, no bounded exponent), and type (FP)_∞ must be defined per the statement as the trivial ℤG-module ℤ (ℤG = MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) admitting a (possibly infinite-length) resolution in which every module is finitely generated and projective — this is not in Mathlib and needs a new definition; note FP_∞ implies finitely generated, so the finiteness cannot be dropped to the (false) Burnside problem.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot with the same shape: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G → (FP_∞ predicate) → Finite G. The FP_∞ predicate in c01/c03/c04/c08 is the most direct: existence of a CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution (ℕ-indexed chain complex of projective objects with a quasi-isomorphism to Z in degree 0, i.e. an exact ⋯ → P₁ → P₀ → ℤ → 0 of unbounded length) of the trivial ℤG-module ℤ in ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G), with Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) on every term. I verified in a scratch file that MonoidAlgebra.single g 1 acts as the identity on (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule, so the module really is the trivial one; categorical projectivity in ModuleCat.{0} over a Type-0 ring coincides with Module.Projective (ModuleCat.IsProjective.iff_projective). Periodic = Monoid.IsTorsion (no bounded exponent), polarity: answer(True) = positive answer. c03 was chosen over the equivalent c01/c04/c08 because it additionally ships a fully proved @[category test] lemma isTypeFPInfty_unit showing the trivial group satisfies the definition (a satisfiability check of the bespoke predicate). c02/c05/c06 (Rep ℤ G-based) and c07 (letI augmentation module) are also correct but more roundabout.

claims.decomposer_note: Existence question the statement names as 'related' rather than as the main problem: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ (G finitely presented); it is logically independent of the primary question (finite presentability gives only FP_2, and FP_∞ groups need not be finitely presented), Mathlib has no finitely-presented-group predicate (would need e.g. a finite generating set with finitely many relators via PresentedGroup), and the expected answers have opposite polarity (a positive primary answer vs. a witness for this one), so care is needed with answer(True)/answer(False).
claims.reviewer_why: All candidates state ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsFinitelyPresented G (conjunction, not implication), with answer(True) meaning a witness exists — opposite polarity to the primary slot, as intended. The IsFinitelyPresented definitions (Fin n generators + Finset/finite Set of relators, or a Finite type of generators + finite Set of relators, up to MulEquiv) are all equivalent and standard. c03's version (∃ n, ∃ rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)), Nonempty (PresentedGroup ↑rels ≃* G)) is used, with its API lemmas (isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup, of_mulEquiv); I added c04's API lemma IsFinitelyPresented.fg (finitely presented → Group.FG), adapted to c03's definition, and confirmed it compiles.

namespace Kourovka.«6.3»

open CategoryTheory

/-- The trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$, on which every element of $G$ acts as the
identity, as an object of the category of `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`-modules. -/
noncomputable abbrev trivialModule (G : Type) [Group G] : ModuleCat (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) :=
  ModuleCat.of (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (Representation.trivial ℤ G ℤ).asModule

/-- A group $G$ is *of type $(FP)_{\infty}$* if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group

  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

/-- The group ring $\mathbb{Z}[1]$ of the trivial group is isomorphic, as a module over itself,
to the trivial module $\mathbb{Z}$ via $r \mapsto r \cdot 1$. -/
noncomputable def trivialModuleUnitEquiv :
    MonoidAlgebra ℤ Unit ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra ℤ Unit]
      (Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModule :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective
    (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton _ _ ((Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv.symm 1)) (by
    constructor
    · intro r s h
      simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply] at h
      apply_fun (Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv at h
      simp only [Representation.asModuleEquiv_map_smul] at h
      simp [Representation.asAlgebraHom_def, MonoidAlgebra.lift_apply, Representation.trivial] at h
      rw [Finsupp.sum_fintype _ _ (fun _ => rfl), Finsupp.sum_fintype _ _ (fun _ => rfl)] at h
      simp only [Fintype.sum_unique] at h

      refine ⟨MonoidAlgebra.single ()
        ((Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv z), ?_⟩
      simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply]
      apply_fun (Representation.trivial ℤ Unit ℤ).asModuleEquiv using LinearEquiv.injective _
      simp only [Representation.asModuleEquiv_map_smul]
      simp)

/-- The trivial group is of type $(FP)_{\infty}$: the trivial module $\mathbb{Z}$ is itself a
finitely generated free $\mathbb{Z}[1]$-module, so $0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z} \to 0$ is a
resolution. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isTypeFPInfty_unit : IsTypeFPInfty Unit := by
  haveI : Projective (trivialModule Unit) :=
    ModuleCat.projective_of_free
      ((Module.Basis.singleton Unit (MonoidAlgebra ℤ Unit)).map trivialModuleUnitEquiv)
  refine ⟨ProjectiveResolution.self _, fun n => ?_⟩

  | zero => exact Module.Finite.equiv trivialModuleUnitEquiv
  | succ n =>

      ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
        (HomologicalComplex.isZero_single_obj_X _ _ _ _ (by simp))
    infer_instance

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and finitely many relators is finitely
presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- Being finitely presented is invariant under group isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H)
    (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : IsFinitelyPresented H :=
  let ⟨n, rels, ⟨f⟩⟩ := hG
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨f.trans e⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  refine Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range (e ∘ PresentedGroup.of), ?_, Set.finite_range _⟩
  rw [Set.range_comp, ← MonoidHom.coe_coe, ← MonoidHom.map_closure,
    PresentedGroup.closure_range_of, ← MonoidHom.range_eq_map, MonoidHom.range_eq_top]
  exact e.surjective

/--
Is every periodic group of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ finite?

A group $G$ is of type $(FP)_{\infty}$ if the trivial $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $\mathbb{Z}$ has a
resolution by finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Z}G$-modules; a periodic group is one in
which every element has finite order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.3» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Monoid.IsTorsion G → IsTypeFPInfty G → Finite G := by
  sorry

/--
The related question mentioned in Problem 6.3: is there an infinite periodic group with a
finite presentation?

That is, does there exist an infinite group in which every element has finite order and which
is given by finitely many generators and finitely many relators?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.3».variants.finitely_presented : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧ IsFinitelyPresented G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.3»

items: 'G-module' is read as (left) module over the integral group ring ℤG = `MonoidAlgebra ℤ G`, as is standard for type FP_∞ (Bieri's notes work over ℤG).

A 'resolution by finitely generated projective G-modules' is formalised via Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution` (an ℕ-indexed chain complex of categorically projective objects with a quasi-isomorphism to ℤ in degree 0, i.e. an exact sequence ⋯ → P₁ → P₀ → ℤ → 0), plus `Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) (P.complex.X n)` for every n. Categorical projectivity in `ModuleCat R` coincides with `Module.Projective` (`IsProjective.iff_projective`). The resolution may be infinite in length, as the statement intends.

`IsTypeFPInfty` and `trivialModule` take `G : Type` (not `Type*`) so that the trivial module ℤ : Type and the resolution live in `ModuleCat.{0}`; the conjecture quantifies over `G : Type` per the decomposition table, and finitely generated modules over a Type-0 ring are small, so no generality is lost.
'Periodic' is `Monoid.IsTorsion G` (every element has finite order, no bounded exponent). The conclusion uses the Prop-valued `Finite G`.

Finitely presented is defined with generators indexed by `Fin n` and relators a `Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))`; this is the standard notion and is independent of the choice of finite generating set. The variant quantifies over `G : Type`, which is harmless since finitely presented groups are countable.

Both questions are yes/no questions formalised with `answer(sorry) ↔ …`; for the primary slot `answer(True)` = 'every periodic FP_∞ group is finite', for the variant `answer(True)` = 'an infinite periodic finitely presented group exists' (opposite expected polarity, as noted in the table).

Bespoke definitions were kept in the problem file (the task restricts output to a single file); a reviewer may prefer to move `IsFinitelyPresented`/`IsTypeFPInfty` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as reusable notions.

Extra declarations besides the two slots: one `@[category test]` lemma `isTypeFPInfty_unit` (with auxiliary def `trivialModuleUnitEquiv`) and two `@[category API]` lemmas about `IsFinitelyPresented`, all fully proved, per CONTRIBUTING's request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.
